h: Holding Fast to Shabbos Carries Holiness Into the Week

p: "Fortunate is the man who does this,
וּבֶן אָדָם יַחֲזִיק בָּהּ (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, ב)
and the son of man who holds fast to it" (Yeshayahu 56:2).
as they said in Midrash Rabbah
and as is written in the holy Zohar
that "zos" is called the trait of Malchus,
and that is Shabbos the Queen.
"And the son of man who holds fast to it"
"It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it":
that he hold fast to the words of Torah
and not let his hand slacken from it
(as they said in Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma,
"A parable of one cast into the sea;
the captain held out the rope to him
'Grasp this rope in your hand,'" etc.;
"Hold fast to instruction, do not let go;
guard it, for it is your life."
And likewise, "the son of man who holds fast to it"
that he hold fast to the holiness of Shabbos
and not let it go from his hand:
and keeping his hand from doing any evil,"
as they said in the Mechilta,
that one who keeps Shabbos is assured
that he is guarded from sin.
And it is as it says (Devarim 30:14):
"In your mouth and in your heart, to do it";
and we said that it does not say "and in your deeds,"
for the completion of the deed is from Hashem Yisbarach,
and Hashem Yisbarach wants from man
that he arouse himself with an awakening from below.
And the main thing is "in your heart,"
for the Merciful One wants the heart
וְזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קס סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
and in Zohar III 160, end of amud a):
which is the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer:
and I created Torah as its antidote";
and for this the voice of prayer is needed,
to pray that Hashem not abandon him into its hand.
for the completion of the deed is from Hashem Yisbarach,
that He not abandon him into its hand.
And this is what Rebbi said (chapter 2 of Avos):
and you will not come to sin:
a seeing eye and a hearing ear,
and all your deeds are written in a book."
And why are three things needed?
It would have sufficed to say
"in your mouth and in your heart, to do it."
"and all your deeds are written in a book"
even though the completion of the deed is from Hashem Yisbarach,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין לָאָדָם לִסְמוֹךְ עַל זֶה
nevertheless a person must not rely on this;
rather he must fence himself in,
to guard against all evil with all his strength.
"and all your deeds are in a book," etc.,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְחֶזְקֵאל לב, כז)
along the lines of what is said (Yechezkel 32:27):
"And their iniquities were upon their bones."
And so it is written in the holy Zohar
that from the performance of mitzvos
is made the "garment of the Rabbis,"
for the deed depends on the body,
וְזֶהוּ עוֹר וּבָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁנִי (אִיּוֹב י, יא)
and this is "With skin and flesh You clothed me" (Iyov 10:11):
for the body is called a garment for the soul,
which is the essence of the person,
and from the performance of mitzvos the garment is made.
And this is "and all your deeds are written in a book":
for the book is the person's body,
upon which all his deeds are engraved.
And the Rema included all this
that the great King, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds, etc.,
immediately fear and submission will come to him,
fear and submission are in the heart;
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that it not be against the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
שֶׁכָּל אָדָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לוֹ יִרְאָה
when every person of Yisrael has fear,
for then they are called "those who fear My Name";
וְאֶל זֶה אַבִּיט אֶל עָנִי וּנְכֵה רוּחַ
"But to this one will I look, to the poor and broken of spirit,"
which is expounded (at the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah)
שֶׁאָז כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עָנִי וּנְכֵה רוּחַ
for then all Yisrael are poor and broken of spirit,
and that corresponds to "in your heart."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר חֵלֶק א לב, א)
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom
"Yaakov is the rope of His inheritance" (Devarim 32:9),
for he holds the rope so that it not be severed,
so that no one of Yisrael can
be severed from the holiness of Yisrael
that is "the son of man who holds fast to it":
that we be able to hold fast to the holiness of Shabbos,
so that it avail also for the coming weekdays;
וְאָז שׁוֹמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע
and then "keeping his hand from doing any evil"
that all deeds be according to His will,
And so we say at Havdalah in the prayer:
"Begin for us the coming days," etc.,
for it corresponds to the trait of Malchus,
opposite which is the Name Adnus,
"And if I am a master, where is My fear?"
And we ask regarding the coming weekdays
that they be joined to the holiness of Shabbos,
